text.p: Germany's Astrid Kumbernuss confirmed her superiority in the women's shot put on Thursday by retaining her world title against some tough opposition.
Kumbernuss, 27, has lost only once in her last 70 competitions and again did not falter when the pressure was on.
She launched the shot out to 20.59 metres in the first round, enough to take the lead, and produced the winning effort of 20.71 one round later.

"Compared to Gothenburg and Atlanta, this was the more difficult competition," Kumbernuss said. "Here life was more difficult. It was a close competition and I always knew that if I won it would only be by a matter of centimetres."
In fact only five centimetres separated her from the Ukrainian silver medallist Vita Pavlysh.
Pavlysh recorded 20.57 in the second round and put all her energy into a final attempt but the shot landed just short at 20.66.
"I saw Pavlysh as a better athlete to anything I have seen in the last two years," said Kumbernuss, the Atlanta Olympic gold medallist added.
"I noticed in qualifying how determined she was, how her jaw was so tense. It helped me get motivated although I'm a little irritated that she did not bother to congratulate me after I won."
Kumbernuss put down her failure to achieve the big distances she had achieved earlier in the season to nervousness.
"I was more nervous than I have ever been before a competition. I hardly got any sleep last night."
However, she said she knew she was unbeatable thanks to her lucky golden weight lifting belt which was made for her after her last one broke in Atlanta.
"It's a sort of talisman but now I'm not going to wear it any more, just keep it in my bag at competitions."
Behind the leading pair, a separate duel developed for the bronze medal.
Germany's Stephanie Storp eventually finished third with her first round effort of 19.22 but China's Huang Zhihong, the 1991 and 1993 world champion, pressed her hard throughout.
